name: Groovy Palette & Frames
description: Thirty-one more entries on the COLORS row -- Amiga Workbench, the C64 boot screen, a Virtual Boy, fuchsia, vaporwave, and two that MOVE: RAINBOW turns the whole picture through the spectrum, ACID lets every rung drift on its own -- plus eight new borders for every text box and menu. Press A on OPTION -> COLORS (or, on Gold, OPTION -> COLOR) and the menu lifts off the game: the palette name and nothing else, left and right to walk the list, previewed on the running game. USE ADVANCED rides the engine's own per-tile colorization instead of replacing it -- the pokered-gbc pack on Red/Blue/Yellow, Gold's own GBC palettes on Gold -- so a palette recolours dozens of colours on screen rather than four. A palette now keeps colours APART rather than washing them into one hue: the blend runs in HSV, so a scheme governs brightness and tints what is already grey while a colour the cart chose deliberately keeps its own hue. On Gold the eight frames join Gold's own FRAME row instead of overriding it -- one ladder of sixteen -- and text boxes finally take the scheme there, as they always have on Gen 1. The one gap: Gold's title screen and Gold/Silver boot cinema keep their own pre-rendered art (the same boundary its DMG and CLASSIC color modes already live with) and pick up the scheme from the first menu or map onward.
